definition: A federal law enacted in 1988 that prohibits companies providing video content from disclosing customers' personally identifiable information — including what videos they watch — to third parties without the customer's written consent. Violations carry a minimum of $2,500 in statutory damages per violation.
examples: Salazar claims that 247Sports violated the VPPA by allowing the Meta Pixel to send his user ID and video-watching history to Facebook without his knowledge.
